angle: Mechanisms for conversational memory at a fixed evidence-token and inference budget: (1) memory unit and source representation, (2) complementary candidate generation, (3) neighbour and session expansion, (4) selection that keeps every supporting fact, (5) fixed-budget RAG vs long-context comparisons and ordering, (6) time-aware retrieval. Sources are mostly authors' arXiv papers. I read the tables in the page images for LongMemEval, LoCoMo, Mem0, SeCom, SetR and Lost-in-the-Middle. Other numbers came from arXiv HTML through a summarising fetch tool and are marked as not image-verified. No local compute was run and no datasets were downloaded. The fetch tool cached the paper PDFs locally on its own.

items.metric: Gold-evidence recall before vs after truncation to the token budget; LLM-judge accuracy
items.value: LoCoMo: grep + NER candidate pool recall 98.6%, but with no reranker only 22.5% of gold evidence survives truncation to the budget. A cross-encoder moves mean gold rank from 195 to 8. Accuracy 91.9% (indexed) at 3,141 average tokens vs full-context 26,792. LongMemEval-S (500): 88.4% index-free at 3,392 tokens. Ablations: stronger reranker (MiniLM to mxbai-large) +6.0 pp; ColBERT RRF +0.5 to +1.2 pp; PRF + entity query expansion neutral on short histories, +9.2 pp on long ones

key_takeaways: Memory unit: keep verbatim rounds or turns as the stored value and add extracted facts to the index key; do not replace the text. LongMemEval_M, round value, Stella: R@10 goes from 0.692 to 0.784 and GPT-4o top-10 QA from 0.670 to 0.720. Facts alone as the key give R@10 0.654, and a summary-only key collapses session QA to 0.252. Fidelity-Before-Structure: extracted artifacts lose to verbatim chunks by 15.9 points on LoCoMo (categories 1-3) and 22.0 on LongMemEval-S; temporal 31.2 vs 50.2. Giving artifacts a matched budget (k=60) recovers only about 1 point. The exception is facts as the value on multi-session aggregation (LongMemEval Figure 5).

Candidate generation: fold the expansion into one key rather than fusing separate rankings afterwards. LongMemEval Table 10: rank merging gets R@10 0.568 vs 0.784 for key merging (round, +fact). BM25 plus dense helps where lexical cues matter: on LoCoMo, weighted z-score fusion gives Hit@1 0.752 vs BM25 0.640, with RRF lower at 0.718; the biggest gains are multi-hop (+17.4) and temporal (+16.2). On LongMemEval-S the gain is small or not significant, and MEMTIER's RRF reached only +0.03 on 100 questions with a -0.125 knowledge-update regression. No controlled HyDE result exists on LoCoMo or LongMemEval; the nearest evidence is an RL rewriter (PPRO, -1.9 F1 when removed) and SmartSearch query expansion (+9.2 pp on long histories).

Neighbour expansion is the best-measured way to recover all the evidence. LazyMem, top-50 messages ±w turns: complete-evidence coverage goes 0.950 to 0.980 on LongMemEval and 0.781 to 0.889 on LoCoMo, and judge accuracy +0.08 / +0.05, saturating at w=2. CueMem reports -9.7 on LoCoMo without turn-graph expansion (unverified). No primary paper compares expansion against simply raising k at the same token count; that is the key missing control.

Selection: pointwise cross-encoders cut both ways. They help a lot when the first stage has high recall but poor order: SmartSearch grep candidates, where only 22.5% of gold survives truncation without reranking and mean gold rank moves from 195 to 8. They hurt when reordering an already-fused shortlist (MiniLM on LoCoMo: Hit@1 -6.9 pp, CI [-9.3, -4.3]) and on multi-hop bridge passages (MuSiQue slice 78.8% to 9.1%, exploratory). Set-wise selection (SetR) beats top-5 reranking with about 2.9 passages (MuSiQue F1 15.43 vs 12.50 for bge-reranker) and raises information coverage from 19.3% to 36.5%, even though its MRR is lower. Recall-preserving reranking inside a fixed top-10 (ConvMemory v2) is a safe pattern.

Recall is not the same as supported answers. Entity-graph retrieval adds +4.7 recall at k=25 on LoCoMo with no F1 change (every CI includes zero). Answer-in-context, meaning whether the answer survives packing, explains ΔR² 0.17-0.27 more than recall. In LongMemEval, 13-25% of all questions have correct retrieval but a wrong answer. Reading format alone (CoN + JSON vs natural-language direct) is worth up to about 6 points with perfect evidence for GPT-4o (0.862 to 0.924) and 8.6 points for Llama-70B.

At a fixed budget, more evidence is not monotonically better. Mem0's RAG grid on LoCoMo (category 5 excluded, gpt-4o-mini judge): k=2 with 256-token chunks gets 60.97, k=2 with 8192-token chunks 60.53, and k=1 with 4096-token chunks 36.84; full context at 26k tokens gets 72.90. LongMemEval long-context loses 30-55% vs oracle, and Zep at 1.6k tokens beats full context at 115k (71.2 vs 60.2, gpt-4o). Raising k is often the single largest gain (Memanto +20.4 pp with confounds; MemMachine +4.2 at k=30, then -2.2 at k=50), which fits the rise-then-fall curve (OP-RAG, Jin et al.). Keep evidence in chronological order (LongMemEval sorts by timestamp; OP-RAG 44.43 vs 38.40 F1) and avoid burying it mid-context (Lost-in-the-Middle 75.8% to 53.8%).

Temporal: LLM-inferred time-range filtering helps only with a strong extractor. With GPT-4o on the LongMemEval_M temporal subset, round+fact R@10 goes from 0.550 to 0.722; Llama-8B invents ranges and often hurts. TSM without its temporal component: -6.0 on temporal and -2.0 overall. SwiftMem's time index leaves recall flat (~90.5%) and only cuts latency. Verbatim text with session dates keeps temporal facts that extraction drops (50.2 vs 31.2).

Measurement hygiene. Report recall_any and recall_all separately: the LongMemEval code logs both, the paper says only 'Recall@k', and the official retrieval evaluation skips the 30 abstention questions (470 vs 500). State original vs Sept-2025 cleaned LongMemEval. State whether LoCoMo category 5 is included (1,986 vs 1,540). LoCoMo category IDs are mislabelled in several papers (Mem0 labels, Engram, MemReranker). Judges are not comparable: GPT-4o with LongMemEval prompts vs gpt-4o-mini with Mem0's 'be generous' prompt vs self-judging Llama-70B. SeCom's main LoCoMo numbers use GPT-4-generated QA, not the official QA.

Code availability: MIT for LongMemEval and SeCom; Apache-2.0 for Graphiti and MemMachine; BSD-3 for SetR (evaluation marked 'TBD'); CC BY 4.0 for opsem (the fusion paper, with receipts); cog-canvas ships cached outputs. MEMTIER and CueMem code is not released. Per-question run artifacts were confirmed only for opsem, cog-canvas and em_graph_memory. Anything marked 'arXiv HTML extraction' or primary=false should be checked against the paper before it goes into a ledger.
